title: JNDI name lookup in application code (java)
description: java code performs a JNDI lookup (new InitialContext(payload)). A lookup name that any part of the request can influence lets an attacker choose the naming provider that answers, and older runtimes will then load and instantiate a remote class — the mechanism behind the log4j family of exploits. This lexical rule flags the lookup; the reviewer confirms the name is a constant.
remediation: Keep lookup names as constants, and where a name must be configurable, validate it against a fixed allowlist with a constant name verified against an allowlist before resolving.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: flags every JNDI lookup, including the constant-name lookups that are safe.
